LMP3.title: Inter Europol win the LMP3 finale as RLR clinch the title
LMP3.dek: Smiechowski and Hippe won for Inter Europol from ninth on the class grid, while fifth place was enough for RLR MSport to take the LMP3 championship.

facts.v: RLR MSport’s fifth in class settled the LMP3 title and earned the team an LMP2 entry for the 2019 24 Hours of Le Mans.

chapters.title: Five crews, one title
text: The European Le Mans Series reached its Portimão finale with five LMP3 crews still mathematically alive. RLR MSport’s #15 Ligier of Farano, Garofall and van Uitert led the standings by 14 points over 360 Racing’s #6 of Woodward and Kaiser, and by 15 over the #2 United Ligier of Falb and Andrews. RLR had won twice, at Paul Ricard and the Red Bull Ring, while 360 Racing had finished on the podium without ever winning.

United’s #3 of Wells, Grist and Bell was still in the maths, as were Eurointernational’s #11 and Inter Europol’s #13, though both needed an extraordinary sequence of results. The champion would take an automatic entry to the 24 Hours of Le Mans. At 18 cars, LMP3 was the biggest class in the field. Iradj Alexander returned to Cool Racing’s #4, Maulini joined DKR’s #8 and Benham M. Racing’s #19, Jensen came back to AT Racing’s #9, and Meshcheriakov made his ELMS debut in Eurointernational’s #12.

chapters.title: Légeret takes M. Racing’s second pole
text: Légeret put the #19 M. Racing - YMR Norma on pole with a 1:40.715, only 0.061s quicker than Lahaye in the Ultimate Norma #17, so the front row of the class was all Norma. Jensen was third in AT Racing’s #9, the best of the Ligiers on 1:40.999, with Klein’s DKR Norma #8 fourth on 1:41.157. It was M. Racing’s second pole of the season.

The title contenders had a difficult session. RLR’s #15 qualified seventh, about nine tenths off the pace, 360 Racing’s #6 was tenth and United’s #3 lined up fourteenth in the class. Eurointernational’s #11 ended up last on the class grid, and the eventual winner, Inter Europol’s #13, started ninth.

chapters.title: Van Uitert leads from seventh
text: RLR did not wait. Van Uitert took the #15 from seventh on the grid to the front of the class early on and built a healthy lead. The title favourites needed only to finish in the points, and that was how he drove.

chapters.title: The safety car resets everything
text: RLR still led when Farano took over around half distance, but a safety car period then pulled the field together and cost the #15 several positions. Farano kept it conservative, since a finish in the points was all the championship required.

Elsewhere the title picture simplified. 360 Racing’s #6 dropped out of contention and finished 35 laps down, and Eurointernational’s #11 was not classified after 85 laps. Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen’s #7 Ligier worked steadily up the order.

chapters.title: Inter Europol take the lead and keep it
text: As the closing laps played out, the #13 of Smiechowski and Hippe emerged at the front and held the class lead to the flag. The top four finished on the same lap: Inter Europol, Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen’s #7, United’s #2 and NEFIS by Speed Factory’s #5, all on 132 laps. Garofall brought the RLR Ligier home fifth, one lap further back on 131, which was enough to secure the championship.

chapters.title: RLR crowned, Inter Europol win
text: The #13 won on 132 laps, with the #7 of Noble, Kapadia and Stubbe Olsen second and the #2 of Falb and Andrews third. NEFIS’s #5 was fourth, RLR’s #15 fifth, AT Racing’s #9 sixth and United’s #3 seventh. Jensen set the class fastest lap, a 1:42.259 in the #9. Pole-sitters M. Racing finished tenth in class with the #19, 360 Racing’s #6 was sixteenth and the #11 was not classified.

RLR MSport were crowned LMP3 champions, the team’s first ELMS title in the class, and with it earned an entry to the 2019 24 Hours of Le Mans, in the LMP2 class with the Oreca 07 it had bought earlier in the year. Farano said the entry was what the whole season had been about.

LMGTE.title: Proton’s #77 Porsche wins the GTE finale as the Rodas take the title
LMGTE.dek: Ried, Dienst and Olsen won for Proton a lap clear of the class, while third place for the Rodas’ sister #88 sealed the title ahead of JMW’s second-placed Ferrari.

facts.v: Gianluca and Giorgio Roda became the first father-and-son pairing to win an ELMS title, taking the GTE crown by 7.5 points.

chapters.title: Porsche against Ferrari for the crown
text: Only six GTE cars entered the finale, but the title was still open. Proton Competition led the standings on 80.5 points, with Gianluca and Giorgio Roda, sharing the #88 Porsche 911 RSR with Cairoli, a little over ten points clear of JMW Motorsport’s #66 Ferrari of Griffin, MacDowall and Molina. A podium would have been enough for Proton to win its first ELMS title in eight years, while JMW was trying to defend the crown it won in 2017.

The fight for second mattered too, because the champion and the runner-up in GTE would both receive automatic entries to the next 24 Hours of Le Mans. JMW held that place by only two points over Spirit of Race’s #55 Ferrari of Cameron, Griffin and Scott. If the Rodas finished, JMW needed to win with the Porsche fourth or lower.

chapters.title: Molina takes the point for JMW
text: Molina put the #66 JMW Ferrari on pole with a 1:42.765, a lap that left Olsen’s #77 Proton Porsche 0.308s behind in second. The pole point trimmed the gap to the championship leaders, and Molina said every point counted. Cairoli was third in the #88 with a 1:43.099, so the points leaders started third in the class.
Griffin’s Spirit of Race Ferrari #55 was fourth on 1:43.239, Pera’s Ebimotors Porsche #80 fifth on 1:43.620 and Bertolini’s Krohn Racing Ferrari #83 sixth on 1:44.053.

chapters.title: Proton’s #77 takes control
text: The class order shifted early, with the pole-sitting JMW Ferrari and Krohn’s #83 both taking turns at the front. By the middle of the race Proton’s #77 had taken charge, with Olsen stretching the gap, while Spirit of Race’s #55 and the second Proton Porsche chased and Ebimotors’ #80 ran among the leaders until it stopped.

chapters.title: A lap clear, and the title settled behind
text: A late safety car reshuffled the class, and when racing resumed the order held to the flag: the #77 won on 130 laps, a lap ahead of everyone else in the class. JMW’s #66 took second, with the title-chasing Ferrari pulling clear of the #88 in the closing laps. The #88 finished third, which was enough, and Spirit of Race’s #55 was fourth, just off the podium.

chapters.title: Proton champions, JMW second again
text: The #77 of Ried, Dienst and Olsen won on 130 laps, with the #66 JMW Ferrari second and the #88 third, both on 129. Spirit of Race’s #55 was fourth on 129, Krohn’s #83 fifth on 127, and Ebimotors’ #80 was not classified after 82 laps. Molina set the class fastest lap, a 1:43.386.

Third place gave the Rodas and Cairoli’s #88 the GTE title by 7.5 points over JMW, whose pole point and second place only trimmed the deficit. Gianluca and Giorgio Roda became the first father and son to win an ELMS title together. Proton and JMW, as champion and runner-up, earned the two Le Mans entries on offer, with Spirit of Race missing out.
